title: SMB: Eliminate NBT Session Message
description:
When the "Draw packets using your coloring rules" icon was
pressed NBT's "Session message" text would appear on the first
request in the Packet Detail.

notes.body: mentioned in merge request !20401

I can still get the same issue; it's very slightly more complicated - I have use the same file, filter for smb, and then click on packet 4 (the first one displayed) before disabling or enabling the color filters.

It's just not reliable to use a static variable like this unless it's reset at the end of the frame with `register_frame_end_routine` (in which case you wouldn't really need to track the frame number, just a boolean of whether this was the first SMB packet in the frame). Equivalent to, but maybe cleaner, than a static reset to false at the end of the frame is using p_add_proto_data with pinfo->pool scope.

I can use pinfo->pool with p_add_proto_data() and p_get_proto_data() to detect multiple commands within a single frame, without using any global or static variables. If instead I use register_frame_end_routine(), I would have to use globals. Your thoughts.

I prefer using pinfo->pool with p_add_proto_data() and p_get_proto_data(), if possible. As you say, register_frame_end_routine() is for globals which we prefer to avoid if we can (but can be a faster way to fix pre-existing code.)

I tried using pinfo->pool with p_add_proto_data() and p_get_proto_data(), but it failed because the values were not maintained between the first and second passes. I also tried changing the scope to packet scope, but p_get_proto_data() does not allow that, and frame scope also failed. Finally, I opted to use GHashtable but that required the table to be global which we wanted to avoid. We also found that register_frame_end_routine required a global. Unless you can recommend another solution, please consider merging this MR.

Hi Cal,

I'm a little confused, because from my understanding you don't actually want to maintain the values between the passes. My conception of the problem:

* Treat certain things (largely adding to the columns) different if this is the first command in a frame (`mult_cmds == false`) or a subsequent command in a frame (`mult_cmds == true`).
* Therefore, at the beginning of the dissection of a frame in any pass, `mult_cmds` should start out as false.
* The first time `dissect_smb` is called for a frame in a pass, when entering it can call something like `mult_cmds = GPOINTER_TO_UINT(p_get_proto_data(pinfo->pool, pinfo, proto->smb, 0))`, and since pinfo->pool data is reset each pass, it will not find anything and it will be 0.
* After doing that, `dissect_smb` can call `p_add_proto_data(pinfo->pool, pinfo, proto->smb, 0, GUINT_TO_POINTER(pinfo->num))`, which will store the current frame number (never zero) in `pinfo->pool` scoped proto data for SMB.
* The next time `dissect_smb` is called for the same frame in the same pass, `GPOINTER_TO_UINT(p_get_proto_data(pinfo->pool, pinfo, proto->smb, 0))` will return the value of `pinfo->num`, which is never 0, and thus `mult_cmds` can be evaluated as true.

Having the values reset between the passes makes this work.

If you don't want to do that, that's fine, but please do add the `register_frame_end_routine` to reset the global.

In the attached image, there are 7 Create_AndX requests in the same frame. Note that frame 3  has the FID and the Pathname, which I don't want. I want the first to look like the 2nd through 7th request with the addition of "Request" on the 1st one. The only way to eliminate the FID and Path is to have multi_cmds equal to TRUE in the second pass. Will 'register_frame_end_routine()' provide that capability? 
  
![25-07-17--0906-28PM](/uploads/2084d491a6b922583000215a6efea65b/25-07-17--0906-28PM.png)

> The only way to eliminate the FID and Path is to have multi_cmds equal to TRUE in the second pass.

Sorry, I think we may have been using different terminology.

A "pass" refers to each time a frame is completely dissected. If there are multiple PDUs of a protocol in a single frame, that dissector will be called multiple times in a single pass. There are multiple passes when a frame is completely dissected again, for example to fill in the columns, or when jumping from frame to frame in the GUI to display the tree. One reason for multiple passes is because a request frame can't know in what frame the response occurred without being dissected a second time.

Under this terminology, you do not want or need `multi_cmds` to be TRUE in the second pass. You want `multi_cmds` to be FALSE the first time `dissect_smb()` is called for the frame in a pass, and `multi_cmds` to be TRUE on all subsequent times `dissect_smb()` is called for a frame in a pass. This is true for all passes, whether the first or later.

The routine registered in `register_frame_end_routine()` is called once per pass, at the very end of the entire frame. It is not called after each `dissect_smb()` call, but some time after the last one exits (before `dissect_frame()` exits.) That can do what you want; you can set it to FALSE at the end of each frame, and then set it to TRUE at the very end of `dissect_smb()`. (You also can read it to set another variable that the columns actually use, and then set it to TRUE immediately after reading it; that can work slightly better in the case of exceptions if something higher level that calls SMB catches the exceptions.)

register_frame_end_routine() cannot be used to fulfill the goal for inter-pass persistence.
It runs once per frame, after all dissection passes have completed. It does not run at the end of each individual pass in a way that allows state to be carried forward to a subsequent pass.

Setting it TRUE at the "very end of dissect_smb()" means the state is being changed during dissection. This state change needs to persist so it can be read by subsequent dissect_smb() calls in different passes of the same frame.

I've established that:

- pinfo->pool doesn't persist across passes.
- wmem_packet_scope() caused "invalid wmem scope" errors.
- wmem_file_scope() should work for persistence across passes, but it doesn't. I'm trying to debug that problem.

> register_frame_end_routine() cannot be used to fulfill the goal for inter-pass persistence. It runs once per frame, after all dissection passes have completed. It does not run at the end of each individual pass in a way that allows state to be carried forward to a subsequent pass.

You use `register_frame_end_routine()` only in connection with a global.

You do not need to carry state forward to a subsequent pass, as I have defined pass above. In fact, you *do not want* to carry state forward to a subsequent pass, because there are cases it will not work to carry state forward to a subsequent pass. Sometimes (as in the case with the columns I demonstrated before) the same frame is dissected twice in a row in two different passes. This can happen if someone clicks in the GUI and selects the first frame (which is dissected to display in the tree) and then changes the columns or colorization status (which redissects all the frames in order to change the columns, starting with the first frame.)

If that happens (that the same frame is dissected twice in a row), then if `last_fnum` is carried forward to a subsequent pass, it will have the same value as the current frame number, even at the start of dissecting a frame, in the first message. That will cause the first message to be treated in the columns like how to you want to treat the second and later messages.

You said,"you use `register_frame_end_routine()` only in connection with a global. That is exactly the reason we started down the path of changing my code. It uses globals as does register_frame_end_routine(). We want a method to eliminate all globals.

The scenario you mentioned of a user hitting the colorization status button works with my code. I have tested multiple scenarios, including that one, and it works fine. What is wrong with my code?
I don't see `register_frame_end_routine` in the current MR or the current master branch. Is it in your local codebase but not the MR?

I don't use register_frame_end_routine() because I don't need or want it.
It does nothing for me. The code works. Please let me know if there is
anything wrong with my code that prevents it from being merged.

The code in this MR does not fix the issue, as I said in the first comment. Sorry if the first comment on this MR was unclear.

Open the file [myandx.pcapng](/uploads/381e9c4dec1f04c9c82bd3833e068963/myandx.pcapng). Filter for smb:

![image](/uploads/b70324d401705fd76eb198d4006b2da4/image.png)

Click on a different packet and then click back on frame 4, so that it is the most recently dissected. Then, click on the icon in the toolbar to enable and disable color filters:

![image](/uploads/30ba5066f8bb6e0fb7535d7018f7d670/image.png)

As you can see, the information in the Info column changes from "Negotiate Protocol" to "Session Message; Negotiate Protocol", because upon doing this, frame 4 is dissected on a non-first pass (`pinfo->fd->visited == true`) with `last_fnum == 4 == pinfo->num`. So `mult_cmds` gets set to true, even though there is only one command in the frame.

This is with this MR.

I see what you're saying. Can you please give me your copy of packet-smb.c
and packet-smb-h with my changes? I didn't keep my old changes and the diff
doesn't have all of them for some reason. Sorry about that.
Sorry, which version of packet-smb.c and packet-smb.h do you need? Are you saying that the changes listed in this MR are wrong or you want some other changes?
The changes are fine, but the author is not. I carelessly updated them without saving first. Can you give the packet-smb.c and packet-smb.h files that you used to produce the failure? Thanks.

You should be able to download them from here, up at the top there's a "Code" button, but here:

[packet-smb.c](/uploads/69d2ae067f2115b0182be225776a36c2/packet-smb.c)
[packet-smb.h](/uploads/dd28caf85736b99d5d22b3393474e516/packet-smb.h)
The solution was simple. I just needed to set mult_cmds to false in each dissection to avoid stale values.
No, that change is preventing multiple commands from being displayed in COL_INFO.

I believe if you use `register_frame_end_routine` and set the global `last_fnum = 0` at the end of every entire frame, it will work as you want. That way when `dissect_smb` is called for the second or later SMB messages in a frame, `last_fnum` will be set to the current frame and `mult_cmds` will end up being set to true, but for the first SMB message `last_fnum` will always be zero and `mult_cmds` will be set to false.

Regarding "for the first SMB message last_fnum will always be zero and
mult_cmds will be set to false." That is one of the problems. I need to
know if multi_cmds was true during the first pass so that, among other
things, I can set how the COL_INFO looks in the second. I believe I have a
solution, which I hope is effective. I'm using
conversation_get_proto_data() to carry over the value of multi_cmds, and I
look for "Session message" within the COL_INFO string. If found, I remove
it. I'm testing all this now.

> I need to know if multi_cmds was true during the first pass so that, among other things, I can set how the COL_INFO looks in the second.

I don't think you do, because in the second pass the frame is dissected exactly the same as in the first pass. You want to set COL_INFO correctly on all passes, including the first.

To be clear on the terminology I am using:

* A single frame can have multiple SMB messages (PDUs.) These are not "passes." In a single "pass" `dissect_smb` is called once for each SMB PDU in the frame. If a frame has two SMB PDUs, then in the first pass dissect_smb will be called twice. In the second and later passed, dissect_smb will again be called twice.
* A "pass" is each time all the protocol layers in the entire frame is dissected. This happens once or twice for TShark, and twice at file loading time for Wireshark, plus an additional time for each time a packet is selected in the packet list, to fill in columns, etc. Each time a "pass" occurs, dissect_smb() is called once for each SMB PDU in the frame, just as in the first pass. (pinfo->fd->visited changes, but that does not affect this.)

For the first SMB message in a frame, you want mult_cmds to be false. For the second and later SMB messages in a frame, you want mult_cmds to be true. This should be the case in every pass. In every pass of the same frame, mult_cmds should be false when dissecting the first message and true on subsequent times dissect_smb is called.

You do not, as far as I can see, need to preserve any information about mult_cmds between passes. You want to preserve it between calls of dissect_smb in the same pass of the same frame, for different messages in the frame.

The reason I need to know beforehand that multiple commands were found is
that the first request that is seen will display something like (The
following each have a request followed by a Close (0x4567) request)

Close FID 0x4567"
rather than
"NT Create AndX Request (0xa2) FID: 0x00a4; Close FID 0x4567".
The problem is that the Close request becomes so fA

(Continued from above) The problem is that the Close request becomes so far away that the user doesn't see it. This has happened to me several times in my career. Notice that the Close looks fine because it knows there are multiple commands. It's the first request that's the problem. Does it all make sense now?

OK, but the current code of yours that was committed and is in current master isn't doing this at all, you agree? It's *not* preserving `mult_cmds` across passes. `mult_cmds` is always false on the first request if `pinfo->num != last_fnum`, which is true the vast majority of the time (exceptions including cases where the column colorization is changed that I demonstrated above as an example of an unlikely situation.) Are you saying that the *current* COL_INFO display is wrong in the typical case with the current code, after your previous commit, when just considering "normal" dissection and not 

If so, then yes, you would need to store information at the file scoped level. You would also, unavoidably, have COL_INFO be different in the first pass (unobserved in Wireshark but the typical output from TShark if `-2` isn't given) than on subsequent passes.
